content.label: This is by far one of the most beautiful games I’ve ever seen. On top of that, the storyline is just good light-hearted fun.

Otherwise, it’s a terrific game!

This game is so much of what I love... tiny little toy boxes full of possibility. The look of the game is absolutely gorgeous with tons of intricate detail, and I wish it felt half as good play. The “hold to place” mechanic is not at all intuitive (I keep trying to tap to place? or something?) and half the time I find it nonresponsive, and the camera often feels quite limiting. Doing anything with speed (I’m stuck on a mud level rn) is finicky and difficult. If just a few of the control things were tweaked I’d be raving, but as of now I just have a thumb cramp.

At one point a piece fell off the board and the puzzle was unsolvable requiring me to restart the level.  At another point I am presented with 4 spots and 4 identical orange pieces and the puzzle just repeats endlessly without feedback or clues.  The puzzles don’t really rotate and the interface seems clumsy.

Great game but I wanted more levels. What was not explained is that this is a strategy game more than it is a “building” game. Love the graphics. Cute at times but was highly disappointed and sometimes frustrated at the lack of angles and line of sight. 

It took some levels to realize you have to make it from point A to point B. Outside of those complaints I was thoroughly immersed in the mixture of ease and difficulty.
Supper annoying to play

title.label: Great graphics but I’m not sure why

content.label:
Is this a game, a puzzle, or a demo? I am very impressed with the graphics but the gameplay isn’t clear and the goals are never mentioned. You can zoom and pan the board you’re playing, but as soon as you take your finger off of the screen, it snaps back to its original position. This make continued gameplay kind of boring and tiresome. I’m at level 3 and I need to do something, but I’m not sure what, and honestly I no longer care. There’re no hints or any incentive to play on to the next level.
Again, great graphics, but the urge to return to the game is a resounding “Meh”.

title.label: Mobile Version of Captain Toad Treasure Tracker

content.label:
I went into this expecting for it to be closer to a kid’s game than a full fledged puzzle game. I was very wrong. From the simplicity of not having menus, easy going tutorial, simple controls, relaxing music, and the attention to detail in every level makes this feel like a testament that it doesn’t have to be a AAA game to be great.

My only complaint is that it was over fairly quickly. I’m hoping for new content down the road. I would gladly download it again to play more.

I started out the game interested. I enjoyed it thoroughly at first, although I felt that it was rather annoying that there were no hints when you got stuck on stuff. I usually ended up getting it after a little while though.
The graphics are quite good and you do get a hang of the controls after a little while. It’s an original and entertaining puzzle game, but there was one thing that ruined it for me.
I had gotten to maybe the 2nd to 4th area when I turned off my iPad to do something else. When I came back my progress had been reset.
I decided to keep playing and got a lot farther on. I was feeling satisfied so I again stopped playing for a few hours.
When I opened the app again I was at the beginning of the mud part.
I was really annoyed at this point. I decided to delete the app. Although I’d be happy to play it again with an updated saving system, having to repeatedly redo levels is not what I want to have to do.
Surprising find. Please make more levels or a part II and III and IV...
This game is beautiful. The graphics are stunning, the details are amazing and the game play is elegant. The only criticism is that it ended too quickly. All in about 45 minutes of game play

title.label: Excellent, but a little too short

content.label:
I thoroughly enjoyed playing this. As a lego fan myself, building my way through this adventure was filled with moments of wonder and awe. It brought me back to easier, less complicated days. I would continue to play but alas, you can literally finish it in less than one sitting. 

Overall, it’s a very, very well-crafted game that delights the young and old alike.

Great looking game that feels mostly like a proof of concept.

The puzzles never become truly challenging and the game can be completed in less than two hours with no real replay value.

Controls feel very clunky. The "long press to place" functionality is frustratingly inconsistent and straining on the fingers.

Worth a play through, but by no means a great game.

This is one of and maybe even the best Apple Arcade games. The graphics were amazing and the soundtrack was beautiful. It touched me when the dad had to leave and I cried. But it was way too short. Please add more levels and I will add my final star. (Also loved loved LOVED the part where the little light brick logo was a vital piece to complete the level.)

This is a very nice puzzle game, cute and I liked guessing what to do in each level. However, the controls are clunky and difficult to actually get pieces where you want them, and you can’t actually rotate your view, despite it appearing as if you can (you get a bit of rotation as long as you aren’t actually trying to do anything; in other words it looks cool but is useless). Worse, I ran into a level where speed matters - a level like that, the pieces need to be easier to move and place or there should be more time. It’s very frustrating when I know what to do and how but actually getting it done is so annoying I just don’t care anymore. This game has a lot of potential. It superficially looks similar to Monument Valley but to those comparing them, this game is not even close to as good or polished.

title.label: Beautiful game undermined by poor controls

content.label:
Builders Journey is a beautiful game in every way: the minimalist scenes, thoughtful music, and overall story arc manage to provide a complex world that provides a highly engaging experience. Tragically, the experience is largely overcast by an unreliable and borderline hostile control scheme. Because of this, most levels took on a imbalance of spending a moment figure out what to do and minutes trying to make the controls accomplish what should have been a simple task.

With different controls, the game would have been a pure delight. As is, however, it teeters between light-fun and rage-inducing.

title.label: Intricate and fun, but too short

content.label: I had fun solving each level, everything is very neat to look at but I just wish there were more levels. It took me 2 days to beat this game

I love Apple Arcade. It’s got something for everyone and it’s really inexpensive.
This game is *beautiful* and smart and fun but also kind of meditative while not being annoyingly easy OR too hard to be fun.
It’s really really great. BUT it has one fatal flaw.
Now, I see people complaining about the controls — I agree they could be a little better but it’s in no way something that I would take off points for. They’re not ~perfect~ but they’re certainly not an actual issue.
I also see some people complaining about some of the puzzles/levels being too hard. That’s crazy. UNLESS you like your puzzle games to be entirely unchallenging so you can just go through the motions of doing the puzzles without really thinking. This is totally not a ~hard~ game. You just have to actually think for a minute and use some trial and error sometimes.
THE PROBLEM IS:
This game. Is SO SO SHORT!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
It almost feels likeeee a super-deluxe version of a demo or something.

I just checked my usage to make sure, I’m not exaggerating whatsoever. Honestly this is probably conservative because I know there were at least a couple of times that I got busy and set it down for a few minutes without closing it or shutting my phone off.
LESS THAN 2 HOURS !
L E G O !
A P P L E !
Honestly kinda shocked they didn’t make a longer game than this.
But!!
It’s still worth playing — it really is great.
Just don’t start getting all cozy with it like you’re gonna be playing this thing for weeks or anything like that.

I have to say this was a wonderful Little game is it short yes captivating most definitely

title.label: A lovely combination between Lego and Monument Vally

content.label:
This is a game about a journey between a father and a son. The story is told in the Monument Vally style. The puzzle is designed based on the nature and variety of Lego bricks. The game starts by building a sand castle, then follows the story, you will be quested by building bridges and so on. 

The video game gives Lego bricks new life in an amazing digital world. For instance, mud bricks will actually flow and sunk like in real world. Light burb bricks will actually lit up. 

The puzzle design is great, but because of the nature of Lego, the bricks that the game provide sometimes are not straight forward enough to understand. Specially in the bridge building puzzle, I took me a while to solve it. 

The story telling is engaging. The most memorable moment by far is the father is forced to work therefore has to leave his son play along. The game will let you to repeatedly do some boring brick building to exchange some credits. In the mean time, your son has to build the half finished castle by himself. 

The control is the flaw of the game. Switching between different bricks, hold to drop and left up operation often conflict with each other.  Because of the camera angle and no other visual assistants, it’s really hard to tell where will be the brick be actually dropped. 

With all things considered, this is the type of game that I will keep playing until see the end of the story.

Beautiful game!
Reminiscent of Monument Valley in its simplicity, art, sounds, and music. 
A charming experience with the only setback being its brevity. PLEASE EXPAND!!!!

A few years ago I got a good deal on a large Wall-E Lego set and it transported me right back to my younger years. It was fun and challenging to put together, and the whole experience awoke the inner child in me. Seeing the finished product was so satisfying. In fact he’s still on my bookshelf on constant lookout to make sure my inner child doesn’t go back to sleep.

Then in walks this new game to the Apple Arcade. It’s a stunning, much more mature and refined reinvention of the Lego game franchise and it’s breathtaking. No hokey Marvel tie-ins, no goofy characters. Think Monument Valley with 3D graphics and dynamic lighting that is so beautiful you’ll stop playing just to take it all in (fun tip: splash the “water” around for a surreal experience). It had the same effect my Wall-E Lego had on me, capturing my attention in a way very few things can manage.

It’s a frustratingly short experience, but absolutely worth your while. I hope Lego realizes the potential here and expands this into a new franchise. Even the short playthrough was captivating and moving enough to melt me; I uttered an audible warm-hearted squeal when the little guy found his hat again. Please Lego, for the love of all things holy, expand this into a full length game.
